# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. This file is
the agent ENTRY document: the harness merges it into the system prompt with
a ~19 KB entry budget, so it must stay small enough to be fully visible.
Ceiling: **≤ 300 lines / ≤ 20 KB** — enforced by
`scripts/check_agents_md_size.sh` (pre-commit hook via `ci_fast_gate.sh` +
the CI `static` job). Subsystem essays live in `docs/` — index:
`docs/README.md`. Keep entries factual: paths, commands, invariants.

## Module map

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph CORE["SDK - flutter_agent_harness, pure Dart (lib/)"]
        AI["ai: providers, agent loop, sessions, compaction"]
        TOLS["tools: approval, redact, hashline, memory"]
        HOSTS["hosts: shared wiring, messaging, a2a, hub"]
    end
    subgraph PKG["packages/ - sibling Dart packages"]
        FAUI["fa_ui: widgets incl. trajectory"]
        DAP["dap_hub, fa_llm, fa_llm_mock"]
    end
    CLI["fa CLI - bin/ + lib/src/cli: TUI, slash commands, headless"]
    APP["Flutter app - flutter_app/: desktop, mobile, web shells"]
    EXT["Browser extension - browser_ext/ + lib/src/browser + serve_bridge"]
    OFFICE["Office add-in - office_addin/ + FA_HOST=office host"]
    GOLDEN["UI golden & styles - golden tests, themes, ui tests"]
    NETW["fa_network - external Go backend + network clients"]
    CORE --> CLI
    CORE --> APP
    CORE --> EXT
    PKG --> APP
    PKG --> CLI
    APP --> OFFICE
    CLI --> NETW
    APP --> NETW
    EXT --> NETW
    GOLDEN --> APP
    GOLDEN --> FAUI
```

## Project layout — one line per subsystem

Full subsystem reference: `docs/agents/sdk-subsystems.md` (SDK) +
`docs/agents/flutter-app-subsystems.md` (app/packages/repo-level).

**SDK core (`lib/`, pure Dart):**

- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers, session modes, per-tool overrides, critical-bash interceptor, per-turn grants.
- `lib/src/tools/` — `ask`/`request_secret`/media tools, `read` selectors + archives + sqlite, background shell jobs, availability + load modes.
- `lib/src/env/` — `ExecutionEnv` impls: `LocalShell` (setsid, killTree, drain caps, self-signal immunity), session-correlation vars, in-memory default.
- `lib/src/agent/` — FinalizeGate, tool pairing, session image registry.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — trajectory ledger core; goldens under `test/trajectory/goldens/`.
- `lib/src/redact/` — layered secret redaction (prompt, tool args, output, logs).
- `lib/src/hashline/` — `[path#TAG]` patch language (SWAP/DEL/INS, stale-tag rejection).
- `lib/src/compaction/` — branch summarization + AutoCompactor → policy: `docs/compaction.md`.
- `lib/src/lsp/`, `lib/src/mcp/` — `lsp` + MCP protocol tooling (lazy servers, pure-Dart transports).
- `lib/src/model_roles/` — roles/fallbacks/keyring/watchdogs + provider catalog; `lib/src/ttsr/` — streaming-interrupt rules.
- `lib/src/skills/`, `lib/src/prompts/` — skills discovery; AGENTS/CLAUDE/GOAL/DESIGN auto-merge into the system prompt.
- `lib/src/task/`, `lib/src/messaging/`, `lib/src/session/attach/` — subagents, inbox fabric, attached sessions → `docs/subagents/README.md`.
- `lib/src/memory/` — long-term memory (hosted `flutter_agent_memory` package) → pitfalls: `docs/memory-churn.md`.
- `lib/src/a2a/` — Agent2Agent client/server/manager (`fa serve --a2a`).
- `bin/fah.dart` + `lib/src/cli/` — the `fa` CLI: REPL, slash commands, headless/serve modes → `docs/agents/cli.md`.
- `lib/src/cube/` — fa_cube sandbox profiles → `docs/cubes.md`; `lib/src/cli/hep.dart` — HEP event protocol → `docs/hep.md`.
- `lib/src/web_search/` — `web_search` (DDG keyless → keyed providers); `tool/fa-clip/` — native macOS pasteboard helper.

**packages/ + app shells:**

# pr-2348: ci(release): tag-run release-leg reds reach ci-red-report (752-754 class)

## Description

Fixes #2332

## The amplifier gap (the one fleet-executable piece of #2332)

The v1.0.752/753/754 tag runs went RED — `Build native binaries` (all 5 legs), `Build web SPA bundle`, `Build Chrome extension`, `Advance vpinned marker` all failed — yet **no issue was ever auto-filed**. Root cause of the reds (notes body >125k chars 422-ing the lazy draft create, then swallowed by `|| true`) is fixed owner-side in #2339. This PR closes the visibility hole that let three releases vanish silently.

## Why the reporter was blind

`ci-red-report` keyed on `needs.quality-gate.result == 'failure'` alone. Since the gh-1801 rework, the release train hangs **after** quality-gate: `binaries`/`web-spa`/`build-extension` need it (not the reverse), and `release-provenance` → `release-asset-smoke`/`installer-smoke`/`install-pin-bump`/`train-draft-guard` hang off those. On 752/753/754 quality-gate was SUCCESS while the run was failure → the `if` was false → skip → no tracker item. The job's own comment claimed "quality-gate aggregates every leg ... covers the whole matrix" — that assumption went stale with the train reorder.

## Change

- `ci-red-report`: `needs` + `if` widened to the whole release-train tail — `binaries`, `web-spa`, `build-extension`, `release-provenance`, `release-asset-smoke`, `installer-smoke`, `install-pin-bump`, `train-draft-guard` — each ORed on its **direct** `result == 'failure'` (fa#456 transitive-skip lesson).
- `push` event gate + `always()` preserved: PR-dispatch failures stay PR-visible; the reporter exists for the tag flow whose reds live only in the tag-filtered Actions tab.
- New guard `test/ci_red_report_release_legs_guard_test.dart` pins the contract at YAML level (repo pattern, cf. `ci_main_push_retired_test.dart`): the coverage set is **derived from the live needs graph** (seeds = the three quality-gate children, closure = everything transitively downstream), so a future release-tail leg added without reporter coverage fails the test; AC1 pins the push/always gate, AC3 pins per-leg direct keying, AC4 rejects phantom needs keys.

## Validation

- `dart analyze test/ci_red_report_release_legs_guard_test.dart` — clean (standalone SDK 3.14.0 in-worktree).
- `dart format` — clean.
- Targeted `dart test test/ci_red_report_release_legs_guard_test.dart` — 4/4 pass.
- Guard bite check: reverting ci.yml to the un-widened needs makes AC2/AC3 fail (repro of the 752-754 class), restoring the fix goes green.
- ci.yml YAML parses under `package:yaml` (the test itself loads it); every needs key verified against the live job list.

Skipped a separate always() aggregator job — the widened needs/if is the smaller diff and costs no extra runner spin-up on tag runs.

integration:
    name: Provider smoke (LLM, tag-only)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: quality-gate
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    # Same !cancelled() pattern as the release/binaries jobs (fa#456).
    # #1368: the gate check reads the dart_ok OUTPUT, not the aggregate
    # result — a platform-only red (Windows build, PTY leg) used to skip this
    # smoke transitively and with it the publish job (the v1.0.519-521
    # starvation). dart_ok=false (a red package leg) still skips it: the
    # publish it gates cannot run anyway.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.outputs.dart_ok != 'false' &&
      github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    env:
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@2286a0c042b44434fe26d292bbce8d34f7ec662b # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      # gh-2072 (review thread 6): this job had NO pub get at all — the
      # prewarm below reads .dart_tool/package_config.json and hard-failed
      # on every fresh checkout, i.e. every v* tag run would red this leg
      # (and publish waits on it). Every other root-package leg already
      # carries the explicit pub get; this was the exception.
      - run: dart pub get
      # Issue #551: the ONLY tag-only LLM job — a small provider smoke.
      # `--tags "integration && llm"` selects the real-provider files
      # (anthropic / google / openrouter / ollama round-trips; copilot,
      # chatgpt-codex and subagent-real-model self-skip without their
      # creds). The 50-file integration suite itself runs per-PR now
      # (integration-mock + nightly pty-integration): tag CI no longer
      # gates releases on it, publish waits on this smoke instead.
      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-
      - uses: ./.github/actions/sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm
      - name: dart test --tags "integration && llm"
        run: dart test --tags "integration && llm"

  js-ext-integration:
    name: JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, quality-gate]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 25
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@2286a0c042b44434fe26d292bbce8d34f7ec662b # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

    name: Auto-release (tag cut)

    # GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never trigger the tag-scoped publish/binaries
    # jobs (gh-1172); the App no longer needs the main-ruleset bypass (no
    # branch push), but remains the release-path actor (gh-1402).
    # Scheduled runs catch up commits that outpaced the coalesce window.
    # !cancelled() + explicit gate check: GitHub propagates "skipped"
    # TRANSITIVELY through an always()-job's needs graph. quality-gate uses
    # if: always() and its needs include path-gated legs (perf-gate etc.)
    # that skip on ordinary pushes — without !cancelled() this job was
    # force-skipped on EVERY run since the perf gate landed (fa#456),
    # silently killing auto-release for a week. The explicit result check
    # keeps the gate red-line: no release on a failed quality gate.
    # workflow_dispatch reaches this job ONLY through an explicit input gate
    # (gh-1172 round-2 BLOCK): this is the repo's dispatch-only CI — the SM
    # runs `gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <pr-branch>` with no inputs, so a
    # bare dispatch arm would execute the dispatched (PR-head) ref's
    # auto_release.sh with the App's tag-push credentials. releaseDryRun
    # exercises the rollout switch (AC1 — any ref, never pushes);
    # releaseDispatch on refs/heads/main is the manual catch-up release.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' &&
      (github.event_name == 'schedule'
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.releaseDryRun == true)
      || (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && inputs.releaseDispatch == true)) &&

      group: release-main
      cancel-in-progress: false

    # checkout App token EXCLUSIVELY, so this job's GITHUB_TOKEN never needs
    # write — on a dry-run dispatch of a PR head (AC1, any ref) that keeps
    # the job's own token read-only, leaving no write-capable credential in

      # may not depend on the script under test honoring the flag. The real
      # arms (schedule, releaseDispatch — gh-1537 retired the main-push
      # trigger, so there is no push arm) see a non-true releaseDryRun
      # and mint as before.
      - uses: actions/create-github-app-token@64ab729a6294000f5aa4a4bc0b73d1f32bc45510 # v3.3.0
        id: app-token
        if: inputs.releaseDryRun != true
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          # Least privilege (gh-1172 round-2 review): contents:write covers
          # the tag push, nothing else. gh-1801: auto_release.sh no longer
          # creates the GitHub Release (an asset-less create publishes an
          # empty `latest`) — the tag-run binaries job owns creation.
          permissions: contents:write

          filter: blob:none
          # App token (not GITHUB_TOKEN) so the pushed tag triggers the
          # tag-scoped publish/binaries jobs — GITHUB_TOKEN pushes never
          # trigger downstream workflow runs.
          # Dry-run dispatch: the mint above is skipped, its outputs are
          # empty (falsy) and checkout falls back to the plain GITHUB_TOKEN
          # (read-only per the job permissions block).
          token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}

          RELEASE_DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event.inputs.releaseDryRun == 'true' && '1' || '0' }}
          # gh-1801 (rework): no GH_TOKEN is exported here anymore —
          # auto_release.sh no longer calls `gh` at all (the asset-less
          # create published an empty `latest` and broke `fa update`; the
          # binaries job owns creation, draft-first). The tag push rides
          # the checkout App token above (gh-1172).
        run: bash scripts/auto_release.sh

exit 1

  # Every failing TAG run must reach a human-facing tracker item the
  # moment it goes red (user ask 2026-09-17): PR-dispatch failures are
  # visible on the PR itself, and gh-1537 retired the post-merge main CI
  # run — so the only `push` events this workflow ever receives are v*
  # tag pushes (release flow), whose reds used to live only in the Actions
  # tab. Files/updates one issue per red run, always assigned to
  # ai-teammate.
  # gh-2332 (the v1.0.752/753/754 class): keying on quality-gate alone went
  # stale when gh-1801 moved the release train AFTER the gate — binaries/
  # web-spa/build-extension hang off it and release-provenance hangs off
  # them, so a red train never touched quality-gate's verdict. Three tag
  # runs went red with quality-gate green: no draft, no release object, no
  # issue — invisible unless someone scrolled the tag-filtered Actions tab.
  # The needs below cover the whole release tail and the if ORs each leg's
  # result; the fa#456 transitive-skip lesson still applies — key on
  # direct results, never transitive skips. Pinned by
  # test/ci_red_report_release_legs_guard_test.dart.
  ci-red-report:
    name: CI red → issue (ai-teammate)
    needs: [quality-gate, binaries, web-spa, build-extension, release-provenance, release-asset-smoke, installer-smoke, install-pin-bump, train-draft-guard]
    if: ${{ always() && github.event_name == 'push' && (needs.quality-gate.result == 'failure' || needs.binaries.result == 'failure' || needs.web-spa.result == 'failure' || needs.build-extension.result == 'failure' || needs.release-provenance.result == 'failure' || needs.release-asset-smoke.result == 'failure' || needs.installer-smoke.result == 'failure' || needs.install-pin-bump.result == 'failure' || needs.train-draft-guard.result == 'failure') }}
    permissions:
      issues: write
      contents: read
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: File or update the red-run issue
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          failed=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID/jobs?per_page=100" \
            --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name] | join(", ")')
          title="[ci-red] $REF failed"
          url="https://github.com/$REPO/actions/runs/$RUN_ID"
          body="**Failed jobs:** ${failed:-unknown}
          **Run:** $url

          Auto-filed by the ci-red-report leg; assignee ai-teammate. Closes manually when the ref goes green."
          existing=$(gh issue list --repo "$REPO" --state open --label ci-red \
            --json number --jq ".[0].number // empty")
          if [ -n "$existing" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$existing" --repo "$REPO" --body "$body"
            echo "commented on #$existing"
          else
            gh issue create --repo "$REPO" --title "$title" --body "$body" \
              --label bug --label ci-red --assignee ai-teammate
          fi

#    release-event option (owner verified the pub.dev console). The old
    #    release arm made the release-event twin of every tag ATTEMPT the
    #    publish whenever the push twin had not uploaded — pub.dev rejected
    #    the token's event claim and the leg died "Authentication failed!"
    #    (exit 65) on every release since the gate graph grew legs that can
    #    redden the push twin. The v0.1.370-402 era this arm once covered
    #    (API-created lightweight tags with no push event) is gone: every tag
    #    is PAT-pushed annotated (gh-1522: the auto_release.sh App-token tag
    #    push), so the push twin

    #    daily verifyPubDev leg alarms «only release-event run(s)» loudly.
    # 2. The gate is dart_ok — the pure-Dart package verdict quality-gate
    #    exports — NOT the aggregate result. A red native binary/PTY leg must
    #    never hold a Dart package hostage (v1.0.520's push twin: publish
    #    skipped off a red pty-integration shard). The Provider smoke stays a
    #    hard gate (#551): needs.integration.result == 'success'.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.quality-gate.outputs.dart_ok == 'true' &&
      needs.integration.result == 'success' &&
      github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    concurrency:
      # push + release events both fire for PAT-pushed tags; serialize the
      # double-fire so the loser no-ops on the already-published guard below
      # instead of racing dart pub publish (version already exists → red).
      # #1368: only the push twin can publish now — the group stays as a
      # belt-and-suspenders guard for re-pushed tags.
      group: publish-${{ github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      id-token: write # OIDC — pub.dev verifies the GitHub identity, no secrets
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # A tag is a release announcement: if pubspec says publish_to: none,
      # failing LOUDLY is correct (#554) — a green skip is how pub.dev went
      # 35 versions stale unnoticed. Removing the flag from pubspec re-enables.
      - id: gate
        name: Publish gate
        run: |
          if grep -Eq '^publish_to:[[:space:]]*none' pubspec.yaml; then
            echo "::error::pubspec.yaml sets publish_to: none — a tagged release cannot reach pub.dev. Remove the flag from pubspec.yaml, or stop tagging v* releases (see #554)."
            exit 1
          fi
          # gh-1452 + gh-1522: pub.dev server-rejects the upload when the
          # PACKED changelog is at/over its 262144-byte content cap
          # (v1.0.538 died mid-upload). The repo CHANGELOG.md is
          # CURATED-ONLY and is NOT what pub packs — the staged changelog
          # is trimmed under the cap by stamp_staged_release.sh before
          # upload — so an over-cap repo file must never kill the release
          # train (that is the exact #1452 class gh-1522 retired). Warn
          # loudly here; the HARD gate is the staged re-measure ahead of
          # `dart pub publish`.
          if ! bash scripts/check_changelog_size.sh CHANGELOG.md; then
            echo "::warning::CHANGELOG.md is at/over the pub.dev 262144-byte cap — the staged (published) changelog is trimmed to fit, so this release proceeds, but archive the tail to CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md (gh-1452)."
          fi
          echo "publishable=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@2286a0c042b44434fe26d292bbce8d34f7ec662b # v1
        if: steps.gate.outputs.publishable == 'true'
        with:
          sdk: stable

      # gh-1522: the repo pubspec carries the 0.0.0-dev placeholder — the
      # tag is the version. Guard the invariant instead of comparing the
      # tag to the placeholder: the committed pubspec must still BE the
      # placeholder (a hand-bump desyncs the tag↔staged-file invariant the
      # stamper relies on), and the staged version must equal the tag.
      - name: Verify committed pubspec carries the placeholder (publish job)
        if: steps.gate.outputs.publishable == 'true'
        run: |
          tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          placeholder=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')
          if [ "$placeholder" != "0.0.0-dev" ]; then
            echo "::error::committed pubspec.yaml version is '$placeholder', expected the 0.0.0-dev placeholder — the tag is the single source of truth (gh-1522); a hand-bump desyncs the staged stamp. Revert pubspec.yaml."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "tag=$tag placeholder=$placeholder"

      # setup-dart (sdk >= 3.13) provisions a publish-scoped credential for
      # the whole job: it exports PUB_TOKEN and registers
      # `dart pub token add https://pub.dev --env-var PUB_TOKEN`, so EVERY
      # pub.dev request — including `dart pub get` metadata reads — carries
      # the publish token. pub.dev rejects it on metadata reads
      # ("depends on ... which doesn't exist (authorization failed)",
      # exit 69; tag v0.1.340, run 34503923233). Resolution must run
      # unauthenticated: strip the credential, resolve, restore it only
      # for the publish step.
      - name: Strip publish credential for dependency resolution
        if: steps.gate.outputs.publishable == 'true'
        run: dart pub token remove https://pub.dev || true

  # gh-1625: dedupe the release-event twin of a tag run. The v* tag push
  # fires the full quality gate by design (the release pipeline keys on
  # the tag and the gate runs BEFORE anything publishes — gh-1537/gh-1172);
  # the `release: published` event for the SAME tag fires a second,
  # identical gate (observed on v1.0.580: push run 38687023638 in_progress

  # concurrency group below — the 35-40 min gate ran twice per release).
  # This pre-check mirrors `release-pending` above: it runs on EVERY event
  # (no job-level if — a skipped pre-check would empty its output and the
  # implicit-success() default would force-skip every leg that needs it)
  # and short-circuits in the script (scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh,
  # fixture-self-tested in Static gates):
  #   release event AND a CI run for the same tag ref from the push event
  #   with conclusion == "success" (FAIL-CLOSED, gh-1625 review: only a
  #   GREEN push gate dedupes — behind the shared ci-<ref> concurrency
  #   group the push twin is already completed when this check executes,
  #   so a failed/cancelled push run degrades to the full-gate safety net
  #   below and the twin goes red on the same commit, attaching nothing)
  #   within the last 6h → dedupe=true: every gate leg ANDs
  #   `needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'` into its `if` and
  #   skips. The twin keeps only its release-specific legs —
  #   binaries-attach (idempotent --clobber upload, last wins),
  #   release-provenance signing and installer smoke; web-spa/publish

  #   twin already attached/published.
  #   no recent push run (release cut on an OLD tag, or a tag the release
  #   created itself — API-created tags fire no push event) → dedupe=false:
  #   the full gate runs exactly as before; that path stays the safety net

  # `gh run list` — an API error degrades to the full gate with a loud
  # warning, never to a skipped gate; the pre-check never reddens the run.
  # AC3: non-release arms short-circuit in the script BEFORE any API call.
  # The concurrency rule below is untouched: the release twin still queues
  # behind the push twin (tag runs are never cancelled mid-flight) — it
  # just no longer re-runs the gate when its turn comes.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  release-dedupe:
    name: Release dedupe check (gh-1625)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read # gh run list — the push-run lookup for the tag ref
    outputs:
      dedupe: ${{ steps.check.outputs.dedupe }}
    steps:
      # The check runs a REPO script — a hosted runner's empty workspace
      # has no scripts/ and the first cut (no checkout) died with
      # `bash: scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh: No such file or directory`
      # (exit 127) on every arm, cascading into a red Quality gate (runs
      # 38696670029/38696668627, on a plain workflow_dispatch arm). The
      # check step itself is UNCONDITIONAL (no job-level if — a skipped
      # pre-check would empty its output), so the checkout must be too:
      # every arm that runs the step needs the file present. A shallow +
      # blobless fetch costs seconds inside the 5-minute budget — the
      # price of keeping the decision extracted to a script that the
      # static gate fixture-self-tests (the alternative, inlining like
      # release-pending, would orphan the selftested script; release-
      # pending stays checkout-free only because its logic IS inline).
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          filter: blob:none # the check never reads blobs — one gh run list
      - id: check
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh

arguments.content:
🚨 **BLOCKING: the coverage set still misses the live tag-run legs that can redden the run — the 752-754 silent-vanish class stays open on the pub.dev publish path**

The widening covers the artifact-train tail, but on a `v*` tag push, `quality-gate` has more children than the three artifact jobs, and none of the others are in `needs`/`if`:

- `integration` — needs `quality-gate` (ci.yml:4237), tag-scoped `if` (ci.yml:4248-4250), no continue-on-error. The **hard gate** for publish ("The Provider smoke stays a hard gate (#551)", ci.yml:4345). A provider-outage red here reddens the run while quality-gate is green.
- `publish` — needs `[quality-gate, integration]` (ci.yml:4320), push-tags-only `if` (ci.yml:4346-4349), no continue-on-error. This is the leg that actually publishes to pub.dev; its own comments document real reds (v0.1.340 exit 69 "Authentication failed!", v1.0.538 died mid-upload). A red publish = the release didn't publish, run is red — and under this PR **no tracker item is filed**.
- `js-ext-integration` — needs `quality-gate` (ci.yml:4286); on a tag push `release-pending` outputs `pending == 'true'` (non-schedule arm short-circuits to pending) and `dedupe != 'true'` (push arms short-circuit to false), so it **runs on tag pushes** and can fail (network quickjs fetch, qjs suites) — ci.yml:4289.
- Also uncovered and tag-run-reddening: `watchdog` (needs ci.yml:4146, tag-arm `if` ci.yml:4150 — the gh-2290 degraded-runner retrigger for releases) and `step-timings` (ci.yml:4066-4067, telemetry; its own comment documents a single 502 reddening the leg).

Each of these reproduces exactly the class this PR fixes: run red, quality-gate green, `ci-red-report` skips, no issue. That contradicts the contract stated in this very job's header (ci.yml:5462-5463): **"Every failing TAG run must reach a human-facing tracker item the moment it goes red"** — and the PR description's own claim that the needs "cover the whole release tail".

The new guard cannot catch this because `_trainSeeds` is hardcoded to the three artifact jobs (test/ci_red_report_release_legs_guard_test.dart:40); the transitive closure only extends **downstream of the seeds**, while `integration`/`js-ext-integration`/`publish` are **siblings** of the seeds (and `watchdog`/`step-timings` are not downstream of `quality-gate` at all).

Suggested fix:
1. Derive the required coverage set from the graph instead of a seed list: every job that can run and fail on a `push`/`refs/tags/v` run — i.e. the transitive closure of `quality-gate` plus the un-aggregated tag legs (`integration`, `js-ext-integration`, `watchdog`, `step-timings`) — and require each of them in `ci-red-report`'s `needs` + a direct `result == 'failure'` OR clause. Exclude `release` (schedule/dispatch-only, ci.yml:5262-5266) and `binaries-pr`/`binaries-smoke-gate` (PR/dispatch-only) with a documented reason, the same way `ci_main_push_retired_test.dart` derives its gate closure.
2. Add the five legs to `needs` and the `if`.

The publish path is the worst one to leave blind: a silent pub.dev publish failure is precisely the "three releases vanish" incident this PR exists to prevent recurring.

arguments.content:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: two of the eight new OR clauses are unreachable — `needs.web-spa.result` / `needs.build-extension.result` can never be `'failure'`**

Both legs carry **job-level** `continue-on-error: true`:

- `web-spa` — ci.yml:4731, and its own comment states the consequence: "Job-level continue-on-error reports the job (and its check) as SUCCESS … **Downstream needs see success**" (ci.yml:4726-4728).
- `build-extension` — ci.yml:4857 ("continue-on-error keeps the check green").
- `release-provenance` confirms it: it needs both "**for ordering only**" (ci.yml:4952-4953).

So `needs.web-spa.result == 'failure'` and `needs.build-extension.result == 'failure'` in the new `if` (line 5482) are dead code: those results are structurally `'success'` even when the builds fail. This is deliberate workflow design (additive assets must not hold the release hostage), so nothing is missed functionally — the 752-754 red sources (`binaries`, `install-pin-bump`) do arm the reporter. The problem is the false contract:

- AC3 of the guard (test/ci_red_report_release_legs_guard_test.dart:111-127) pins these two dead keys with the reason "a leg failing while quality-gate is green must arm the reporter (gh-2332)" — for these two legs that is **never true** and never was. A future maintainer reading the guard will trust coverage that structurally cannot fire.
- Keeping both legs in `needs` also delays every report: the job's `if` is evaluated only after **all** needs settle, so a `binaries` red now waits for the 30-minute-timeout web/extension legs before the issue files.

Suggested fix: drop the two dead clauses from the `if` (and from `needs` if the settle-latency isn't wanted — that also requires adjusting AC2, which currently mandates them via the seeds), and scope AC3 to legs that can actually report `failure` — or, if web/extension coverage is genuinely desired, emit a real failure signal (a step-level output or a small hard-fail aggregator) and key on that. Either way, the guard should assert the reachable contract, not the unreachable one.

None carries `continue-on-error`; a red in any of them reddens the run while quality-gate stays green → the reporter skips → the exact 752-754 silent-vanish class recurs, against the contract in the job's own header (ci.yml:5462-5463: *"Every failing TAG run must reach a human-facing tracker item"*). The guard can't catch it: `_trainSeeds` is hardcoded (test:40), so the closure only extends downstream of the seeds — the escapes are *siblings*. The incident's actual red sources (`binaries`, `install-pin-bump`) do arm the reporter, so the fix works — but AC3 pins these dead keys as the coverage contract, and their `needs` entries delay every report until they settle. Fix: drop the dead clauses and re-scope AC3, or give the legs a real failure signal.

**Digest**: `.github/workflows/ci.yml:5482` — fold the ~370-char single-line `if` with `if: >-` like every neighboring long-if job (readability only).
